readiness: Do not order yet: 2 blockers, 12 major items
headline: The ASIC board exists only as the near board of each stacked pair and has no fabrication package of its own, so it cannot be ordered as drawn. The blockers are ASIC-01 (no far board, and two stacked copies would drive the same 24 output wires) and ASIC-02 (the blind and buried via set has no workable lamination sequence); twelve major items follow, chiefly the missing and unspecified decoupling (ASIC-05, ASIC-06), the wire-bond finish and pads (ASIC-07, ASIC-13), the undecided thickness (ASIC-08) and the die and probe fit (ASIC-11, ASIC-12). First design the far-board variant and agree a buildable stack (thickness, via spans, bondable finish) with the fabricator, then restore the decoupling with real values and make a fabrication package from the current board.

findings.title: Only the near ASIC board of each stacked pair exists; stacking two copies would tie chip outputs together.
findings.what: Each FPGA-LDO port (J3 or J4) carries two stacked ASIC boards, a near board and a far board. On this board J3 and J4 are wired straight through, both chips drive odd-row 'direct' pins, and the 22 T_ pins only pass through to the next board with no chip on them. The far board must therefore be a different design whose chips drive the T_ pins, and no such design exists in the workspace. Stacking two copies of this board ties two chips' outputs to the same wires (output contention, where two drivers fight over one line) and leaves the T_ lines undriven.
findings.where: ASIC board J3 (DF40C-80DS, bottom) and J4 (DF40C-80DP, top). Chip 1 (U01_BCD1): D<1..8> on pins 79, 77, 75, 73, 43, 41, 39, 37; READ 35; CLK32MHZ 45; SYNC 47; DISC_OUT 5. Chip 2 (U01_BCD2): data on 33, 31, 29, 27, 17, 15, 13, 11; READ 9; CLK32MHZ 19; SYNC 21; DISC_OUT 3. T_ nets on even pins 10-22, 26-32 and 60-80. FPGA-LDO A and Option B router: J4 even pins to ASIC3/4, J3 even pins to ASIC7/8; pins 3 and 5 open.
findings.evidence: exports/asic/connectors.csv and netlist.xml: J3 pin n and J4 pin n carry the same net on all 80 pins (2, 4, 6, 8, 24, 58 unconnected) and share the same x/y. Each output net has 3 nodes (J3, J4, chip pin), e.g. /D<1> = J3.79, J4.79, U01_BCD1; all 22 /T_* nets have only 2 (J3, J4). 11 certain outputs per chip (8 data, READ, SYNC, CLK32MHZ) give 22 contending wires that reach the FPGA-LDO board; DISC_OUT on pins 3/5 adds 2 more, but it is unconnected on the FPGA-LDO boards and sits in a separate column of the designer's sheet with its termination undecided. exports/ldo_a and ldo_b_router connectors.csv assign the T_ pins to ASIC3/4/7/8 (e.g. J4.80 ASIC3_DATA1, J4.10 ASIC4_READ). Workspace search (214 .kicad_pcb files in the workspace; 1,106 including ~/kicad_work): only the 4 Nov 'Bottom' board and its copies, including the deck copy, have J3+J4 and T_ nets; the September single-J3 board (sha e01ee641...) and the July Board-1024.zip board (J1/J2) have no T_ nets; 'PCB - Bottom.zip' holds only the same 'Bottom' project. Rotating a second copy 180 degrees is worse: D<5> (pin 43) would land on VDD_DRIVER (pin 38). The deck record says 'Top board ready / Bottom board not ready yet' while the only CAD folder is named 'Bottom'; either way only one variant exists.

findings.title: The ASIC board's via set has 28 crossing span pairs, so no normal lamination sequence can build it.
findings.what: The board uses one via, 0.15 mm drill with 0.25 mm pad, in 17 layer spans: from L1 down to every inner layer and from every inner layer to L10. Sequential lamination (pressing the board in stages and drilling between presses) can only make spans that nest or do not overlap; here 28 span pairs cross, for example 1-9 against 2-10, so at least one via of each pair would need controlled-depth drilling (drilling from the outside to a set depth). That works only to about 1:1 depth to width, and these holes reach 9.6:1. Two same-net via pairs also sit closer than the board's hole spacing minimum, which would need filled and capped vias that the board does not ask for.
findings.where: Whole ASIC board, all layers. 87 of the 133 non-through vias other than 1-2 sit in the J3/J4/capacitor band (y 67.4-73.5 mm). Examples: REF_VCM 1-5 and VDD_DRIVER 6-10 at (136.01, 68.44), 0.070 mm apart; DGND 9-10 and VDD_FE 1-3 at (134.45, 68.19), 0.068 mm apart; same-net pairs VDD_ADC 1-7/7-10 and REF_VDD 1-4/4-10.
findings.evidence: exports/asic/vias.csv and board.json: 501 vias, all 0.15/0.25 mm; spans 1-2 x139, 1-3 x8, 1-4 x8, 1-5 x9, 1-6 x14, 1-7 x17 (7 tagged buried by KiCad), 1-8 x8, 1-9 x24, 1-10 x229, 2-10 x4, 3-10 x4, 4-10 x4, 5-10 x4, 6-10 x8, 7-10 x9, 8-10 x4, 9-10 x8; KiCad reports 0 microvias. Crossing pairs (1-k against j-10 with j<k): 7+6+...+1 = 28. Depths from exports/asic/stackup.txt (0.035 mm copper, 0.1 mm prepreg and 0.1825 mm cores alternating): 1-9 and 2-10 = 1.445 mm, 1.445/0.15 = 9.6:1; 1-7 = 1.093 mm (7.3:1); 1-2 and 9-10 = 0.17 mm (1.1:1); through = 1.58 mm (10.5:1). exports/asic/drc.json hole_to_hole: VDD_ADC 0.0365 mm and REF_VDD 0.0979 mm against a 0.1016 mm minimum. 64 via pairs are closer than 0.326 mm; 18 are different-net pairs on spans that share no layer, so KiCad does not flag them, but the REF_VCM 1-5 and VDD_DRIVER 6-10 ends are separated only by the 0.1 mm L5-L6 prepreg, so a drilling depth error would join two rails. boards/asic/PCB.kicad_pcb: filling no, capping no, plugging no. Reviewers' clash check (tracks, pads and vias; pours ignored): 170 of the 272 non-through vias could become through vias, 102 could not. The June PCBWay set (inputs/asic/pcbway_fab) has only through vias, so this via scheme has never been built.
findings.source: PCBWay capabilities page, Advanced PCB, https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html: item 2 (1+1+...+N+...+1+1 HDI normal, any-layer HDI medium), item 5 (0.20 mm normal minimum mechanical drill), item 6 (aspect ratio 8 normal, 10 high difficulty, over 12 non-standard). The crossing-span rule and the roughly 1:1 controlled-depth limit are engineering judgement; the page does not cover controlled-depth drilling.
findings.consequence: A fabricator will reject the order or quote it as any-layer HDI with a different thin-dielectric, laser-drilled, filled stack, which matches neither the drawn 0.15 mm drilled vias nor the 0.1825 mm cores. Even the 229 through vias at 0.15 mm on 1.6 mm (10.5:1) are high difficulty at PCBWay.
findings.suggested_action: Ask the fabricator which spans and drill sizes it can build on this stack. Then reduce the set to the spans it accepts (for example through vias plus shallow 1-2 and 9-10): 170 of the 272 non-through vias convert to through directly, and the other 102 need local moves.

findings.title: Each near/far ASIC pair shares one SPI data stream, so eight chips get only four configuration streams.
findings.what: Each ASIC chip loads its gains, reference DAC settings and stimulation tables through its own serial (SPI) data lines, SPI_DINL and SPI_DINR. The ASIC board passes no T_ copy of these lines and leaves its spare pins open, so a far board can only reach the near board's SPI wires, and FPGA-LDO A, the Option B router and the Frontend carry only four data pairs. Each far chip therefore gets exactly the same configuration, stimulation tables included, as the near chip below it, and SPI_LATCH and CHIP_RESET are shared by all eight chips. The project's earlier 117-signal baseline had six data streams and a clock per board; the dropped nets are still marked 'to confirm'.
findings.where: ASIC board J3/J4: chip 1 SPI_DINL 59 / SPI_DINR 57, chip 2 SPI_DINL(2) 25 / SPI_DINR(2) 23, CLKH 7, SPI_CLK 63, SPI_LATCH 61, CHIP_RESET 71; spare pins 2, 4, 6, 8, 24, 58. findings.title: The ASIC board places 18 of its 50 schematic decoupling capacitors, two per rail, 5.9-10.8 mm from the dies.
findings.what: Decoupling capacitors are small local charge stores that keep a supply steady when a chip draws current in fast steps. The schematic has 50 but the board has 18, so each of the nine rails keeps exactly two, shared by both dies; 16 sit in a row on the far side of J4 from the dies and C6/C50 sit just east of J4. The cut came in the 2 Nov save that added J4 over the old capacitor area, and the designer's J3 spreadsheet lists exactly these 18, so it looks deliberate, but the schematic was not updated and no ASIC document gives a decoupling requirement. VDD_CGEN has no inner plane, so the far die's VDD_CGEN pin has no local storage.
findings.evidence: exports/asic/summary.txt and drc.json: parity 32 missing_footprint. Placed/schematic per rail (netlist.xml, pads.csv): VDD_FE 2/4, VDD_ADC 2/6, VDD_DRIVER 2/6, DVDD 2/8, REF_VDD 2/8, REF_VCM 2/4, VDD_CGEN 2/2, VDD10 2/6, VSS10 2/6 = 18/50. Nearest same-net die pad 5.9-10.8 mm from each capacitor (e.g. C1 10.15, C7 6.92, C50 5.88 mm), farthest 21.7 mm (C1 to U01_BCD2). Die power pads reach a same-net via within 0.38-0.72 mm, except VDD_CGEN (4.26 mm at U01_BCD2, 13.56 mm at U01_BCD1). exports/asic/zones.csv: VDD_CGEN has only L1 4.8 mm² and L10 2.9 mm², no plane; its trace totals 18.0 mm (L1 17.2 + L10 0.8, mostly 0.2 mm wide), 14.98 mm from the J4 pin at (143.34, 72.36) to the U01_BCD1 pad. Plane capacitance is only tens of pF (VDD_FE L3 over AGND L2: 324 mm², 0.1825 mm, εr 4.5, about 71 pF). Earlier layouts: the single-die board in Board-1024.zip has 48 capacitors at 2.42-8.27 mm; the 17 Sep archive PCB-5 has 50 at 2.31-9.10 mm. KiCad history in 'PCB - Bottom.zip': 50 capacitors at ae1a44a (2 Nov 22:35:48), 18 with J4 added at b6b662e (22:35:53). inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv 'Decoupling caps' column names exactly the 18. FPGA-LDO A and the B router place 1 µF 0402 parts (C51, C53-C57) on six ASIC rails at J3/J4. exports/asic/bom.csv: C1-C50, quantity 50, no values. Back side under the dies: 120 through vias and 63 B.Cu segments.
findings.source: No ASIC datasheet value exists (inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md, U02/U04: fitted R/C population unconfirmed). Design intent in PCB.kicad_sch and the ASIC designer's earlier layouts. Engineering judgement.
findings.consequence: Higher supply and reference noise at the ADC and low-noise front end is plausible but unproven (4-5 µVrms target, 6.5 µVrms measured in ASIC_REFERENCE.md), and the far die's VDD_CGEN sees about 15 mm of thin trace with no local capacitor. Ordering from the schematic BOM buys 50 parts for 18 sites.
findings.suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for the minimum capacitor set and values per rail per die, then either reduce the schematic to the 18 placed parts so parity is clean or add capacitors nearer the dies (at least VDD_CGEN at U01_BCD1). Before using the back side under the dies, check clearance to the lower board's dies and wire bonds in the 1.5 mm stack gap.

findings.title: No ASIC-board capacitor has a value, voltage rating or part number, including four 0201 parts on ±10 V rails.
findings.what: All 50 schematic capacitors carry only the symbol name 'C_Small_US' as their value, with no voltage rating, MPN (manufacturer part number), LCSC number or datasheet, so the board cannot be quoted or assembled from these files. An unspecified 0201 part could be rated 6.3 V or 10 V, which would put it at or above 100 % of its rating, and ceramic capacitors lose much of their capacitance under DC bias. 0201 parts rated 16-25 V exist, so the gap is the missing rating, not the package.

findings.title: Every ASIC bond pad is on the solder-paste layer, and no record specifies a wire-bondable surface finish.
findings.what: All 352 bond fingers (the board pads that the ASIC's bond wires land on) carry solder paste. The board also needs a top-side stencil for 18 0201 capacitors and J4, so a stencil cut from these files would print solder onto the fingers, and a soldered finger cannot be bonded reliably. The surface finish field reads "None", which is KiCad's default; the real finish is chosen on the order form, which is not in the workspace, so nothing records a bondable finish or the bond-wire type it must suit. The mask openings equal the pad size with 0.1016 mm webs, which is a smaller point: the fabricator will probably open the whole row.
findings.where: ASIC board, U01_BCD1 and U01_BCD2 (footprint chip:U01_BCD_OFF_CHIP), all 176 pads each, top side: F.Cu, F.Mask, F.Paste.
findings.evidence: boards/asic/PCB.kicad_pcb read with pcbnew: each U01 footprint has 176 SMD pads (128 at 0.1016 x 0.254 mm, 45 at 0.1016 x 0.635, 2 at 0.2032 x 0.254, 1 at 0.2032 x 0.635), all on F.Cu, F.Mask and F.Paste, with no pad or footprint paste/mask margin; board paste margin 0, pad_to_mask_clearance 0 (line 172), copper_finish "None" (line 169). Pad pitch 0.2032 mm, so gaps are 0.1016 mm (exports/asic/pads.csv). parts.csv, bom.csv and pos.csv list both U01 parts as placed and in the BOM with no DNP flag. The older single-ASIC PCBWay set (inputs/asic/pcbway_fab, 21 June 2026) flashes 177 bond-pad paste apertures and its PCB-job.gbrjob reads "Finish": "None". No record of finish, wire bond or stencil decision in inputs/asic, inputs/notes or inputs/system.
findings.source: PCBWay capabilities page, https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html: ENEPIG and hard gold in the Standard tier, soft gold and wire bonding not listed, green-mask bridge 4 mil normal. IPC-4556 scope (ENEPIG suits soldering and Au, Al and Cu wire bonding) seen only on a reseller page; the standard itself was not read. Otherwise engineering judgement.
findings.consequence: Solder printed on the fingers, or a finish that does not suit the bond wire, would leave the dies unbondable on that build.
findings.suggested_action: Remove F.Paste from the U01 pads (or blank those apertures on the stencil) and mark U01 as not placed by the assembler. Record the bond-wire type and order the matching bondable finish (for example ENEPIG or soft gold) in the order notes.

findings.title: The ASIC board file is a 10-layer 1.6 mm stack, but the recorded choice and the fit models use 0.8 mm.
findings.what: The project record says 0.8 mm was chosen on 6 November and the deck's fit models draw the ASIC board at 0.8 mm, but the board file and its Gerber job still define a 1.6 mm board, so ordering the files as they stand gives 1.6 mm boards. No fabricator has been asked whether a 10-layer 0.8 mm board with this blind and buried via set can be built. Going thinner makes the vias easier (lower aspect ratio, the hole depth divided by its width); the real 0.8 mm risk is nine very thin dielectric layers and the impedance the fabricator can then offer. The J1 side pin clashes in the generic model at both thicknesses.

findings.title: ASIC board tracks, via rings and edge copper are at high fab difficulty, and the via-ring check is turned off.

Copper planes on L1 to L9 and some via pads come to about 0.10 mm from the routed board edge. Also, 272 of the 501 vias are blind or buried (not running through every layer) and use 0.15 mm mechanical holes over about 16 to 18 different layer spans, which needs many lamination cycles and is the strongest open question for the fabricator.

findings.title: Open vias sit inside the DF40 and 0201 capacitor pads, and no via filling or capping is specified.
findings.what: Many vias are drilled straight into the J3 and J4 connector pads and the 0201 capacitor pads. An open via hole inside a pad pulls molten solder down into the hole, which can starve a fine-pitch joint and leave a pin open. The board setup says the vias are not filled, plugged or capped; tenting (covering a via with solder mask) does not help inside a pad, because the pad is open in the mask. PCBWay does sell filled and plated-over vias, so the fix is an order option, not a redesign.
findings.where: ASIC board: J4 (DF40 header, top, pads 0.23 x 0.66 mm), J3 (DF40 receptacle, bottom, pads 0.2 x 0.7 mm), and all 18 placed 0201 capacitors (C1, C2, C4, C5, C6, C7, C14, C18, C19, C25, C26, C33, C34, C41, C42, C46, C48, C50).
findings.evidence: boards/asic/PCB.kicad_pcb lines 172 to 187: tenting yes/yes; covering, plugging, capping and filling no; pad_to_mask_clearance 0. All 501 vias 0.25/0.15 mm (vias.csv). pcbnew overlap check (scratch/verify-asic-f10-files): J4 has 30 through vias and 12 blind vias, every hole inside a pad; J3 has 25 through vias (15 to 16 with the hole in the pad, the rest touching) and 17 blind vias (16 hole in pad); the 18 capacitors have 38 vias, 33 with the hole in the pad, 15 of them centred 1-2 vias. The through vias in J4 pads come out under J3 pads, since J3 and J4 sit at the same XY. Volume: an open 0.15 mm x 1.6 mm barrel holds about 0.028 mm3, against roughly 0.009 to 0.012 mm3 of solder per DF40 joint (stencil thickness assumed). No via-fill specification for this layout exists in inputs; the PCBWay set there is an older through-hole-only layout.
findings.source: Engineering judgement. PCBWay Via in Pad help page, https://www.pcbway.com/helpcenter/ordering_parameter_instruction/Via_in_Pad.html (resin fill with plated cap); Via Filled with Copper page, https://www.pcbway.com/helpcenter/ordering_parameter_instruction/Via_Filled_with_Copper.html (copper-paste fill for 0.1 to 1.0 mm holes in 0.2 to 4.0 mm boards); HDI page, https://www.pcbway.com/hdi-pcb.html (resin fill from 0.254 mm). Hirose DF40 guideline not checked: hirose.com returned 403.
findings.consequence: Open or weak DF40 joints in the board-to-board stack, hidden under the connector body, and tombstoned or poorly soldered 0201 capacitors.
findings.suggested_action: Order copper-paste-filled, plated-over vias (via-in-pad) for the in-pad vias, after the fabricator confirms it covers a 0.15 mm drill in this board, and set filling and capping in the board setup; otherwise move the vias off the pads.

findings.title: The bond-finger opening fits the 8.1 x 7 mm die only if the die is thin, and no file records its thickness.
findings.what: Each die sits in an 8.583 mm wide opening between the inner bond-finger columns, with 8.795 mm from the top finger row to the bottom board edge. One bonding house's guide asks for a die-to-finger gap of 1.5 x die thickness. With the 8.1 mm side across the opening the die must be no thicker than 0.16 mm; with the 7 mm side across it must be no thicker than 0.46 mm, and only if it sits flush with the board edge. Neither orientation keeps all wires in line with the fingers, which matters for gold ball bonding but not for aluminium wedge wire. No file records the die outline, thickness after backgrinding (thinning), pad map, wire type or orientation.

findings.title: Each bond finger has its own zero-margin mask opening, and the fingers are narrower than one maker's rule.
findings.what: Bond fingers are the board pads that the bonding wire from the ASIC die is welded to. On the ASIC board each finger gets its own solder-mask opening exactly the size of the pad, which leaves 0.1016 mm mask strips between fingers with no allowance for the mask shifting during manufacture; the one published wire-bond rule found (Wurth Elektronik CBT) asks for one open block over the whole finger row. The fingers are also 0.1016 mm wide against that sheet's 150 um width, and the side fingers 0.254 mm long against its 300 um drawn length, but that sheet is one maker's guide for its own process and fingers about 100 um wide are often bonded with fine wire, so width and length are a question for the chosen PCB maker and bonding house rather than a shown failure. No bonding house or finger rule is recorded anywhere in the inputs.
findings.where: ASIC board, U01_BCD1 and U01_BCD2 (footprint chip:U01_BCD_OFF_CHIP), F.Cu / F.Mask. Per die: 128 side fingers 0.254 x 0.1016 mm in two columns 0.713 mm apart in x, 0.2032 mm pitch within a column (most inner-column fingers share the outer column's y positions; this is not a uniform half-pitch stagger); 45 top fingers 0.1016 x 0.635 mm at 0.2032 mm pitch (U01_BCD1 row at y 75.36). findings.title: The DVDD and VDD_ADC regulators sit on the opposite ground from the one the ASIC board returns each rail on.
findings.what: On the ASIC board DVDD is decoupled to DGND and VDD_ADC to AGND, but on FPGA-LDO A the DVDD regulator U5 and its capacitors sit on AGND while the VDD_ADC regulator U3 and its capacitors sit on GND; NT1 (a net tie, a deliberate single copper joint between two ground nets) is the only AGND-GND bond on either board. The DC load current does not cross NT1 because of this: a linear regulator's load current returns to its input supply, and its GND pin carries only about 6.5 uA of quiescent current, so DVDD's DC return stays on GND. What does cross NT1 is the AC current drawn from the AGND-referenced capacitors C501, C502 and C54 (about 11 mm of the L2 AGND plane, away from the REF_VDD, REF_VCM and VDD_FE regulators), plus a small offset in each regulator's reference; the worst case is about 6 uV. The original LDO board had the same crossing, and the files cannot show whether the ASIC die bonds AGND and DGND internally.

findings.title: The ASIC power budget leaves REF_VDD and REF_VCM current unknown and may understate peak stimulator current.
findings.what: The ASIC designer's budget sheet gives currents for the four main 1.5 V rails but leaves the two reference rails, REF_VDD and REF_VCM, as TBD. It allows 2 mA per board on the stimulator rails VDD10/VSS10, while 128 stimulators at the 22.5 uA maximum would draw 2.88 mA per chip if all ran at full current at once; the specification does not say whether they can, so this is a worst-case bound, not a contradiction. REF_VCM is made by an LT3042, a regulator that only sources current; whether REF_VCM must also sink current is unknown. The files cannot settle this; the ASIC designer's figures for reference-rail current and direction and for peak stimulator current would.

findings.title: FPGA-LDO A brings the ASIC rails up in a fixed staggered order that has not been checked against the ASIC.
findings.what: All nine ASIC regulators on FPGA-LDO A share one enable signal, so their start order is set only by how fast each one ramps. The TPS7A2015 rails (DVDD, VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, VDD_CGEN) come up fast, while the LT3042/LT3094 rails ramp slowly through the RC formed by their SET resistor and capacitor. Digital and driver rails therefore lead the references by tens of milliseconds and the +/-10 V stimulator rails by about a quarter second. The files cannot settle whether this is acceptable: the ASIC's sequence and powered-off limits are unknown, and only the ASIC designer can say.

findings.title: Panel tabs on the ASIC board's bottom edge would sit on the probe edge, and the left edge is not clean either.
findings.what: An earlier suggestion was to keep the bottom or left edge free for breakaway tabs. Both bond-finger rings are open towards the bottom edge, and the project notes say the probes leave the board at the chip end, so a tab nub, mouse-bite (a row of small holes that lets a tab snap off) or V-score there would sit where the die edge and probe are. findings.title: The Frontend and FPGA-LDO board mate through two DF40 pairs, which Hirose's drawing asks designers to avoid.
findings.what: Sheet 3 of Hirose's DF40 plug drawing asks designers not to put more than one mated DF40 pair between two stacked boards. If the pairs are slightly misaligned, a connector can break during or after mating; Hirose suggests splitting the board instead. The Frontend mates with the FPGA-LDO board through two 70-pin pairs, J1 and J2, in both Option A and Option B. The ASIC joints and the Option B J5 joint each use a single pair, so they follow the caution.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/parts.csv, exports/ldo_a/parts.csv, exports/ldo_b_ldo/parts.csv: the two connectors sit 17.500 mm apart on every board, so nominal alignment is exact; the caution is about tolerance between two rigidly placed pairs. DF40 self-alignment range is +/-0.33 mm in X and Y (DF40 catalog p3). The same issue is also raised in findings/_raw/gapldo_b-gap3-df40-120-drawing.json, rated minor.
findings.source: Hirose drawing EDC3-311351-00, DF40C-*DP-0.4V(51), sheet 3/3, Mating method (4), caution for using multiple connectors; https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=2d&lang=en&num=DF40C-80DP-0.4V%2851%29
findings.consequence: If the two pairs are not coplanar and aligned within tolerance, mating or unmating the Frontend can stress or crack one connector. No mounting feature shares the load.
findings.suggested_action: Ask Hirose whether two DF40C-70 pairs 17.5 mm apart on one board pair are acceptable and what placement tolerance they need; record the answer or a tolerance study.

findings.title: It is not shown that the bonded dies fit in the 1.5 mm gap under the next stacked ASIC board.
findings.what: The two ASIC dies are wire-bonded on the top side of the ASIC board. In a stack they face the bare underside of the next ASIC board, 1.5 mm away (the nominal mated height of the DF40 pair). Die thickness, wire-loop height and any glob top (a blob of protective epoxy over the die and wires) must add up to less than that gap minus tolerance. The workspace does not hold these numbers, so the files cannot settle this; the die thickness and bonding/coating height from the ASIC designer or bonding house would.
findings.where: ASIC board, U01_BCD1 and U01_BCD2, top side, pads x 125.0-145.6 mm, y 75.4-84.0 mm. In Option A this affects the inner board of each pair: board 1 under board 2 and board 4 under board 3. Board 3's die area lies past the FPGA-LDO A edge and faces nothing.
findings.evidence: exports/asic/pads.csv: U01 pad extents x 124.98-145.63, y 75.36-83.96. exports/asic/parts.csv: J3 is the only bottom-side part (y about 71.0), so only bare PCB lies over the dies. inputs/system/README_2026-11-11.md lines 43-53: 1.5 mm DF40 gaps, dies modelled as 0.5 mm boxes, no tolerances modelled. Search of inputs/asic and inputs/system: no die thickness, loop height or encapsulation figure.
findings.source: Engineering judgement.
findings.consequence: If die plus wire loop plus coating exceeds the gap less tolerance, the coating touches the board above or the bond wires are crushed.
findings.suggested_action: Get the die thickness and bonding/coating height from the ASIC designer or bonding house and check the sum against 1.5 mm less DF40 and board tolerances.
